item.title: 9 episode(s) — 8:54am 26/Nov
item.description:
Key Themes:

  • Cost of living and inflation pressures — AM focused on the human impact on households ahead of Christmas, while RN Breakfast and The Quickly analysed the macroeconomic data, RBA rate hikes, and economic recession risks.
  • Liberal Senator Leah Blyth's defection to One Nation — RN Breakfast focused on the political fallout and opposition unity, while The Briefing framed it as part of broader political shifting and parliamentary dynamics.

Interviewees:

  • Andrew McKellar, Chief Executive, Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Bessa Deda, Chief Economist, Westpac (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • David Shoebridge, Greens Senator (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Matt Canavan, Nationals Senator (ABC Radio National Breakfast; The Briefing (Listener))
  • Oliver Nobetau, Pacific Islands program director, Lowy Institute (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Pat Conroy, Minister for Defence Industry and International Development (ABC Radio National Breakfast)
  • Chris Kohler, Economics Correspondent (The Quickly)
  • Marco Alberti, Associate Director of International Engagement and Education, European Space Policy Institute (ABC Radio National Breakfast)

Key Actors:

  • Leah Blyth
  • Pauline Hanson
  • Anthony Albanese
  • Barnaby Joyce

Episodes in this run:

ABC AM: Inflation biting hard ahead of Christmas

  • Christmas inflation squeeze (00:07, 01:21)
    Angle: Struggling households facing a challenging Christmas period due to soaring inflation and economic pressures.
    Voices: Isabella Higgins, host (live); Margaret, self-funded retiree (pre-recorded); Simon Peng, retailer (pre-recorded); Paul Bloxham, Chief Economist Australia, HSBC (clip)
    Tone: Alarmed and sympathetic towards households facing cost-of-living stress, mixed with objective economic analysis.
    Emphasis: Human impact of inflation, cost of basic goods, and broader economic headwinds.
    Placement: Lead item, occupying the entirety of the broadcast segment.
    Evidence: “Many Australians could be facing a challenging Christmas period ahead as new fears of stagflation grip the nation.”

ABC Radio National Breakfast: Economists react to inflation hitting 4.9 per cent

  • Inflation spike and economic outlook (00:02, 03:42)
    Angle: Soaring inflation figures putting pressure on the Reserve Bank and households, requiring productivity boosts.
    Voices: Patricia Karvelas, host (live); Andrew McKellar, Chief Executive, Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (live); Bessa Deda, Chief Economist, Westpac (live)
    Tone: Inquisitive and urgent, pressing economic experts on what solutions exist to fix supply constraints and tame inflation.

    Placement: Lead item.
    Evidence: “There's still significant inflation pressure in the economy, and I think it should ring alarm bells.”
  • Housing costs and inflation (02:27, 01:53)
    Angle: Housing costs and construction issues as major contributors to inflationary pressures.
    Voices: Patricia Karvelas, host (live); Tom Devitt, Senior Economist, Housing Industry Association (clip); Bessa Deda, Chief Economist, Westpac (live)

    Emphasis: Legislative process, political leverage, and policy priorities.
